th.q: Let us think about this parable that the Lord gives us today. How is our life going? What do I prefer? To always accept the Lord’s invitation, or to close myself off in my own things, in my own little concerns? And let us ask the Lord for the grace to always accept the invitation to go to His feast, which is freely given.
th.by: Pope Francis, Homily, Mass at Casa Santa Marta, 5 November 2019

th.q: Sometimes we portray them as great figures, forgetting that for them it all began when, while still young, they said “yes” to God and gave themselves to him completely, keeping nothing for themselves.

He wants to tell you that you are precious in his eyes, that you are unique. No one can replace you in God’s heart. You have a place; you are you, and no one can replace you; nor me, no one can replace me in God’s heart.

How much more, then, must we, who are disciples living in the light of the Gospel, use the goods of this world and our very lives with a view to the true wealth, which is friendship with the Lord and with our brothers and sisters.

Those who serve God become free from wealth, but those who serve wealth remain its slave! Those who seek justice transform wealth into the common good; those who seek dominion transform the common good into the prey of their own greed.

And this love is a gift of Christ, poured out in us by the Holy Spirit. Those who believe in God-Love bear within them invincible hope, like a lamp to light them on their way through the night beyond death to arrive at the great feast of life.

2026-11-09.t: The Dedication of the Lateran Basilica

th.q: At times, one can come across mistrust and hostility. One should not allow oneself to be stopped but rather safeguard the conviction that for God three days are enough to resuscitate his Son in the heart of man.

Rather, we must be aware that in reality we never do enough for God. We must say, as Jesus' suggests: "we are unworthy servants; we have only done what was our duty" (Lk 17: 10). This is an attitude of humility that really puts us in our place and permits the Lord to be very generous to us.
th.by: Pope Benedict XVI, Homily, Foro Italico in Palermo, 3 October 2010

th.q: It is easy to approach the Lord to ask for something, but to return and give thanks...
And the Kingdom of God “is there, hidden in that holiness of daily life, that everyday holiness”. Because “the Kingdom of God is not far from us, it’s close”.
Therefore, brothers and sisters, let us remain vigilant! Waiting for the Lord to come, waiting for the Lord to draw near to us, because he is there, but waiting alert.

When we are “crucified” by pain and violence, by hatred and war, Christ is already there, on the cross for us and with us. There is no cry that God does not console; there is no tear that is far from his heart. The Lord listens to us, embraces us as we are, and transforms us as he is.
And may the Virgin Mary help us to overcome fear (never be afraid of God! Awe, yes; fear, no) and to trust the Lord.
Jesus also passes by in your Life; and when Jesus passes by, and I realize it, it is an invitation to draw near to him, to be better, to be a better Christian, to follow Jesus.

No one asked him for so much, not even the Mosaic law. But the fact is that his encounter with Christ transformed his heart, and then everything changed. Only generosity is so effective that it reveals to us the meaning of our humanity.
th.by: Pope Leo XIV, Address to Members of the National Anti-Usury Council, 18 October 2025

th.q: The message of today’s Gospel is clear: let us not bury the wealth of the Lord! Let us spread the wealth of charity, share our bread and multiply love!
Please, let us ask for the grace to weep. All of us.
th.by: Pope Francis, Address to pilgrims from Bergamo, 23 April 2022

th.q: Jesus had told us that one cannot serve two masters: either God or riches; either God or power.
th.by: Pope Francis, Homily, Casa Santa Marta, 20 November 2015

th.q: God’s love is so great that Jesus does not keep even his mother for himself, giving Mary to us as our mother, in the hour of the cross (cf. Jn 19:27). Only those who live by such full dedication can affirm: “For whoever does the will of my heavenly Father is my brother, and sister, and mother” (Mt 12:50).
It is left to us to respond to him, not with words but with deeds: by choosing the path of effective and generous love for our neighbour we allow him to extend his lordship in time and space.
th.by: Pope Benedict XVI, Address to pilgrims from the Archdiocese of Amalfi-Cava De’ Tirreni, Italy, 22 November 2008

th.q: Let us learn from her: a faith without external frills, but interiorly sincere; a faith composed of humble love for God and for our brothers and sisters.

Jesus’ words, in their prophetic way, attest to the fact that the disasters and sorrows of history will come to an end. At the same time, the joy of those who recognize him as Savior, is destined to last forever.

Dostoevsky wrote: “Have no fear of men’s sin. Love a man even in his sin, for that is the semblance of Divine Love and is the highest love on earth” (The Brothers Karamazov, Part 2, Book 4, Chapter 3). Perseverance is the reflection in the world of God’s love, because God’s love is faithful, it is persevering, it never changes.

If worries weigh down our hearts and induce us to close in on ourselves, Jesus, on the contrary, invites us to lift up our heads, to trust in His love that wants to save us and that draws close to us in every situation of our existence, He asks us to make room for Him in order to find hope again.
Let us not forget that God is preparing for us a future of life and joy.

This is especially true when we feel that our enthusiasm has cooled down. Prayer re-lights it, because it brings us back to God, to the center of things. Prayer reawakens the soul from sleep and focuses it on what matters, on the purpose of existence. Even during our busiest days, we must not neglect prayer.
All these things pass away. Be watchful, the Lord tells us.
th.by: Pope Francis, Homily, Basilica of Saint Peter, 29 November 2020

th.q: He, who alone knows us and who loves us fully, leads us to put out into the deep of life. Just as he did with the disciples who heard him. That is why we need his word: so that we can hear, amid the thousands of other words in our daily lives, that one word that speaks to us not about things, but about life.
Prayer opens us to receiving the gift of God, His wisdom, which is Jesus Himself, in order to do the Father’s will in our lives and thus to find rest in the hardships of our journey.
th.by: Pope Benedict XVI, General Audience, December 7, 2011

th.q: As we savor the grace of the Eucharist, let us commit ourselves to bearing witness to its beauty in our daily actions, beginning with blessing meals at the table with family and friends.

And imagining ourselves there, in His presence, at the threshold of eternity, we make the decision for today. We must decide in this way: always looking to eternity, looking at Jesus. It may not be the easiest, it may not be the most immediate, but it will be the right one, that is certain.
Let us consider whether our prayer is needy and confident: needy, because we tell ourselves the truth, and confident, because we believe that the Lord can do what we ask.
th.by: Pope Francis, Homily at Santa Marta, December 6, 2013

th.q: Instead, we need to pray to the Lord of the harvest. Priority must be given, then, to our relationship with the Lord and to cultivating our dialogue with Him. In this way, He will make us his labourers and send us into the field of the world to bear witness to His Kingdom.

Let us be content with what is essential and make time each day, when possible, for a special moment to pause in silence to pray, reflect and listen – in other words, “to withdraw into the desert”, in order to meet the Lord and remain with Him.
Only God’s love can renew the human heart, and only if He heals the heart of paralyzed humanity can it get up and walk. The love of God is the true force that renews the world.

2026-12-08.t: The Immaculate Conception of the Blessed Virgin Mary

th.q: Dear friends, how great is the gift of the Immaculate Conception, but so also is the gift of Baptism that we have received!
Docility and humility of heart help us not only to take on the burden of others, but also to keep our personal views, our judgments, our criticism or our indifference from weighing on them.
His greatness is different. And let us start again from this originality of God, which shone in Jesus and which now binds us to serve, to love fraternally, to acknowledge ourselves as small.
It will do us good to ask ourselves these questions today. And the last one: am I resistant to the salvation of Jesus?
th.by: Pope Francis, Homily at Santa Marta, October 3, 2014

th.q: We need Elijah’s spirit. He shows us that there should be no dichotomy in the life of those who pray: one stands before the Lord and goes towards the brothers and sisters to whom He sends us.
Silence and sobriety, in words, in the use of things, in the media and social media: these are not just fioretti or virtues; they are essential elements of the Christian life.
“Lord, may prophets not be lacking among Your people!” All of us who are baptized are prophets.
th.by: Pope Francis, Homily at Santa Marta, December 16, 2013

th.q: But this, even the smallest concrete commitment, cannot be made without grace. Conversion is a grace we must always ask for: “Lord, give me the grace to improve. Give me the grace to be a good Christian”.

For this reason, in this Advent season, as disciples of the Lord, we are called to combine our anticipation of the Savior with attention to what God is doing in the world. Then we will be able to experience the joy of freedom in encountering our Savior: “Gaudete in Domino semper – Rejoice in the Lord always” [Phil 4:4].
Matthew’s genealogy, therefore, is not merely a list of generations: it is history brought about first by God, but with humanity’s response.

In this time of grace, let us not waste the opportunity to practice them: forgiving, encouraging, giving a little hope to those with whom we live and those we meet; and renewing in prayer our filial abandonment to the Lord and His providence, entrusting everything to Him with confidence.

Am I able to feel the Spirit’s consolation or am I closed off? Let us ask ourselves, each of us, in an examination of conscience: How is my faith? Is it joyful? Is it open to God’s surprises? Because God is the God of surprises.

Everything that happens demands that we look at the present boldly, with that boldness of him who knows that the joy of salvation takes shape in the daily life of the house of a young girl from Nazareth.

May our “I” not be at the centre, but rather the “You” of Jesus and the “you” of brothers and sisters, especially of those who need a hand. Then we will leave room for the Love that, even today, seeks to become flesh and to come to dwell in our midst.

May we imitate her example of readiness and generosity in the service of our brethren. Indeed, only by accepting God’s love and making of our existence a selfless and generous service to our neighbour, can we joyfully lift a song of praise to the Lord.
th.by: Pope Benedict XVI, Address at the conclusion of the Marian month, May 31, 2008

th.q: May she, Mother of God and our Mother, make us more aware that in having children, parents are acting as God’s assistants. It is a mission that is truly sublime, which makes each family a shrine of life, and it, each child’s birth, awakens joy, wonder and gratitude.

The Lord gives all of us His grace, His strength, so that we may be profoundly united to Christ, who is the cornerstone, the pillar, and the foundation of our life and of the whole life of the Church. Let us pray that enlivened by His Spirit we may always be living stones of His Church.

It is a feast of charity, because the gift of the redeeming Son is realized in fraternal self-giving. It is a feast of hope, because the Child Jesus kindles it within us, making us messengers of peace. With these virtues in our hearts, unafraid of the night, we can go forth to meet the dawn of a new day.

To this day, however, no power can prevail over the work of God. Everywhere in the world, there are those who choose justice even at great cost, those who put peace before their fears, and those who serve the poor instead of themselves. Hope then sprouts, and it makes sense to celebrate despite everything.

2026-12-27.t: The Holy Family of Jesus, Mary and Joseph

th.q: But also marvelling at God’s kindness in walking with us, even though we are not such experts at it. May Mary, Queen of the family, help us marvel. Today, let us ask for the grace of being able to marvel. May Our Lady help us to be amazed at what is good every day, and to know how to teach others the beauty of wonder.

Being obedient to the voice of the Lord by taking his Bride and child to safety, the gesture of Joseph is revealed in all its redemptive significance. In Egypt, the flame of domestic love, to which the Lord has entrusted His presence in the world, grows and gains strength in order to bring light to the whole world.

2026-12-29.t: The Fifth Day in the Octave of Christmas

th.q: And He did not avoid difficulties. Rather, by choosing a family, a family that was “expert in suffering”, He says this to our families: “If you are facing difficulties, I know what you are experiencing. I experienced it. I, My mother and My father, we experienced it so we could say to your family too: You are not alone”!

2026-12-30.t: The Sixth Day in the Octave of Christmas

th.q: And so, just steps from the “Holy of Holies,” the Fountain of Light offers Himself as a lamp to the world, and the Infinite gives Himself to the finite in a way so humble that it almost passes unnoticed.

2026-12-31.t: The Seventh Day in the Octave of Christmas

th.q: The peace of God is born from a newborn’s cry that is welcomed, from weeping that is heard.

2027-01-01.t: Mary, the Holy Mother of God

th.q: Certain that Christ, our hope, is the sun of justice that never sets, let us confidently implore the intercession of Mary, Mother of God and Mother of the Church.

First, that we cannot save ourselves alone: only in God do we find the light of life. And second, that each of us, through service, consistency, humility, witness of life, and always by God’s grace, can be a lamp that shines and helps others find the way on which to meet Jesus.

May His Kingdom grow, may His words come to fulfillment in us, may strangers and enemies become brothers and sisters. In the place of inequality, may there be fairness, and may the industry of war be replaced by the craft of peace. As weavers of hope, let us journey together towards the future by another road (cf. Mt 2:12).

As Christians, therefore, we too must overcome the temptation toward isolation. The Gospel must be proclaimed and lived in every setting, serving as a leaven of fraternity and peace among all individuals, cultures, religions and peoples.

2027-01-25.t: The Conversion of Saint Paul, Apostle
